info.title: higgsfield/higgsfield-wan-3
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "higgsfield/higgsfield-wan-3", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description:
Real wire request for Higgsfield's Wan 3.0 reference-to-video endpoint (alibaba/wan-3.0/reference-to-video). Unlike the Kling family the tier is a BODY field here (`resolution`). Higgsfield documents two rules JSON Schema cannot express and the provider therefore enforces: at least one reference input must be present, and `file_url` and `link_url` are mutually exclusive.
Comfy Router publishes and ENFORCES this schema for `POST /v2/models/higgsfield/higgsfield-wan-3`, which forwards the body below to Higgsfield untranslated. The alternate-provider leg `wan/wan3.0-video?model_provider=higgsfield` is a different route with a different contract: it takes `wan/wan3.0-video`'s own Wan-native body, is validated against that model's authored schema, and is translated onto this wire shape before dispatch. The two bodies are not interchangeable.

example.prompt: Use Image 1 for the character and Video 1 for the camera movement

aspect_ratio.description: Output aspect ratio. `adaptive` lets the model pick one from the input media.

audio_urls.description: Public WAV or MP3 reference URLs, up to 5 files with a combined duration of at most 30 seconds.

duration.description: Output duration in seconds, 2-30. With video input, input duration plus output duration must not exceed 30 seconds — a cross-field rule the provider enforces.

enable_thinking.description: Enable additional reasoning. Higgsfield enables it automatically when `file_url` or `link_url` is supplied.

file_url.description: Public document URL used as context (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, TXT, Markdown). Cannot be combined with `link_url`.

generate_audio.description: Generate synchronized dialogue, ambience, sound effects and music.

image_urls.description: Public reference image URLs, up to 10.

link_url.description: Public web page URL used as context. Cannot be combined with `file_url`.

prompt.description: Text instructions for the output. Reference the supplied assets by order — "Image 1", "Video 1", "Audio 1" — matching the order of the corresponding *_urls array.

resolution.description: Output resolution tier. This is where Wan 3.0 carries its tier — the Kling family carries the equivalent choice in the path.

video_urls.description: Public reference video URLs, up to 5 clips with a combined duration of at most 30 seconds.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Higgsfield's request envelope, returned BOTH by a generation POST (as `{status: "queued", request_id, status_url, cancel_url}`) and by the shared status route, which adds the output once the request completes. Only the video output is modelled here because the two enrolled families are video models; Higgsfield's own shared component also carries image and audio outputs for families Comfy does not enrol.
This is also the Comfy Router output schema for every Higgsfield video id Router publishes — `higgsfield/higgsfield-kling-3-{std,pro,4k}`, `higgsfield/higgsfield-kling-3-turbo` and `higgsfield/higgsfield-wan-3`. All five are SUBMIT-AND-POLL: Router polls the shared status route on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is this TERMINAL document rather than the queued handle the generation POST answers with. A caller therefore reads `status: "completed"` with the download URL at `video.url`; `queued` and `in_progress` are in-flight states Router does not return, and `nsfw`, `failed` and `canceled` are the terminal failures. `url` is required on the video output, so a `completed` carrying no `video` is a contract break rather than a finished generation.

cancel_url.description: Absolute URL used to cancel a request before processing starts.

request_id.description: Stable identifier used for polling, cancellation and support.

status_url.description: Absolute URL to poll until the request reaches a terminal state.

url.description: Download URL of the generated media.
